Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Buyer-side assessment

The Seller’s package shifts substantial completion, valuation and post-completion risk to Wattlebridge. The most important points to resist are the weak closing protections for Bluefen and Riverlark, the treatment of the disclosed liabilities as ordinary or adequately covered, and the proposed blanket limits on claims.

This review is based on the Seller’s update and disclosure letter only—not the full SPA, schedules or underlying DD materials. We should check the operative drafting and source documents before settling positions.

### 1. Liability limits and claim protections

- **General cap: AUD 4.8 million.** This is only 20% of the AUD 24 million price and may be inadequate for a business acquisition. Push for a materially higher general-warranty cap, supported by the diligence and risk profile. Do not let this cap apply to fundamental/title warranties, tax, specific indemnities, fraud or deliberate concealment.
- **De minimis and basket.** The AUD 25,000 de minimis may exclude individually smaller but collectively meaningful losses. More importantly, the proposed basket is **deductible**: the Seller pays only the excess above AUD 250,000. Seek a tipping basket (once crossed, the full amount is recoverable), or at least a lower deductible basket, and ensure related claims can be aggregated.
- **18-month claim period and default time bar for all Claims.** Eighteen months may be too short to discover latent warranty, tax or regulatory issues. Seek longer periods for general warranties and periods tied to the relevant statutory limitation period for tax, title and other fundamental matters. The default rule must not inadvertently time-bar indemnity, debt, purchase-price adjustment or other contractual claims.
- **Fundamental/title warranties.** Reject applying the general cap and time limits to capacity and title. Require robust protection for ownership, valid issue and transfer of all shares, absence of encumbrances, and the Seller’s authority to sell. Negotiate a separate, substantially higher cap—typically up to the price—and an appropriate longer claim period.
- **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to all Claims.** Do not accept a blanket bar on claims of any nature. Preserve claims for fraud, deliberate concealment, specific indemnities, debt and payment obligations, and any agreed price adjustment or completion obligation. Make clear that non-reliance wording does not exclude liability for express contractual representations or fraud.
- **Tax and IP under the general regime.** “Settled” is not a sufficient answer. Tax risks need appropriate tax warranties and, where diligence warrants, a tax covenant/indemnity with tailored caps and time limits. IP ownership, infringement and chain-of-title risks also need meaningful warranty protection and specific remedies where identified.

### 2. Disclosures and Buyer knowledge

- **General data-room and public-register disclosure is too broad.** It could qualify warranties by reference to a large body of material without identifying what the Seller says is disclosed. Resist blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts and public records. Require specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail to understand the nature and reasonably assess the scope of the matter.
- **The letter’s reservations matter.** It expressly does not admit breach, liability, materiality or loss, and says the Buyer must assess the facts against the full agreement. The disclosed matters therefore should not be treated as agreed immaterial or as accepted by the Buyer.
- **Buyer knowledge waiver is overreaching.** Reject “actual or discoverable” knowledge, including advisers’ knowledge and matters discoverable from records. It risks turning diligence access into a waiver. At most, any knowledge qualification should be narrowly defined as actual knowledge of specifically named individuals, after reasonable inquiry, and should not apply to fraud, deliberate concealment or specific indemnities.

### 3. Completion conditions, debt and price mechanics

- **Bluefen is a material customer risk.** The disclosure records roughly AUD 3.6 million FY26 revenue—about 30%—and a change-of-control clause with conditions. The Seller confirms there is no final written consent or evidence that associated conditions are met. “Reasonable endeavours” and deeming the condition satisfied on delivery of consent are inadequate. Make effective consent, satisfaction or waiver of all contractual conditions, and no adverse variation or termination right, a condition precedent. Include a long-stop date and a termination right if it is not satisfied; do not deem it satisfied merely because a document is delivered.
- **Riverlark must be resolved by Completion.** The AUD 3.2 million facility remains outstanding, and no final discharge is in the data room. A release “following Completion” leaves the Buyer exposed to debt and secured-asset risk. Require repayment or refinancing at Completion, an effective lender release and discharge of security, and documentary evidence. Ensure payoff is reflected in the funds flow and debt-free/cash-free mechanics; use escrow or a holdback if any discharge document cannot be delivered simultaneously.
- **Verify the funds flow against the agreed price mechanics.** The disclosure says the AUD 420,000 conditional employee bonuses are omitted. Determine whether they are completion debt, transaction expenses or a price adjustment under the SPA; require appropriate payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs to be included where applicable. No amount should be left as an unallocated post-completion burden.
- **Supplier renewals.** The three AUD 110,000 renewals total AUD 330,000. The documents do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Do not accept the Seller’s label as dispositive. Review the contracts and timing, and ensure any accrued or transaction-triggered liabilities are captured in the completion accounts, debt/expense definitions or a specific adjustment.

### 4. Identified operational and title risks

- **Ironquay IP.** The Seller’s existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, but the disclosed contract makes transfer of Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment, and the AUD 180,000 “open” figure is not independent verification of non-payment. Require verified payment and an effective assignment/transfer of all relevant materials and IP by Completion, with a specific indemnity for loss of rights, infringement or claims arising from the matter. Do not assume a payment-only indemnity cures a title or chain-of-title gap.
- **Export/privacy incident.** DD-006 describes an unintended external email recipient and a possible export of about 1,240 records; access, scope and notification obligations remain unresolved. Its preliminary status is not a reason to dismiss it. Require the full investigation and available evidence, appropriate remediation and any required notifications, plus targeted warranties and a specific indemnity for liabilities arising from the incident. Consider a condition, escrow or retention if the investigation cannot be completed before signing or Completion.
- **Title evidence.** DD-012’s share register is a source, not conclusive verification of all aspects of title. Require customary title warranties and completion deliverables establishing transfer of 100% of the issued shares free of encumbrances, with authority and corporate approvals confirmed.
- **Other contract notices/consents.** The lease disclosure identifies a notification obligation, while Mossvale contains an assignment restriction but does not say share-sale consent is required. Review the actual provisions. Require notices and any consent or confirmation actually required by the contracts, and make clear that the Seller’s disclosure does not itself establish that no action is required.

## Recommended negotiating position

1. Keep Bluefen consent and its conditions as a genuine completion condition; require Riverlark repayment and effective security discharge at Completion.
2. Reconcile the funds flow for bonuses, on-costs, debt, transaction expenses and supplier liabilities under clear price mechanics.
3. Reject blanket data-room disclosure and constructive-knowledge waiver; require specific, fair disclosure.
4. Increase and tailor the liability regime: a higher general cap, a tipping or lower basket, longer claim periods, and separate treatment for title, tax, IP and identified indemnity risks.
5. Preserve fraud, deliberate concealment, specific indemnities and payment/price-adjustment claims from blanket limitations and exclusive-remedy wording.
6. Secure Ironquay IP transfer and targeted protection; investigate and allocate the privacy/export incident risk expressly.
7. Review the full SPA and underlying DD-002 to DD-012 before agreeing that any risk is covered, immaterial or ordinary-course.
